scope: Country-level agricultural production, cereal-yield and food-security evidence. This file is not a calculator profile and does not authorize country activation.

currency.name: Congolese franc
currency.note: Currency identification only. No verified dated farm-gate prices or enterprise input quotations are recorded in this file.

geographic_coverage.note: National aggregates conceal major differences between provinces, agroecological zones, crop seasons, transport corridors and conflict-affected areas. Any eventual farm budget must be localized.

evidence.source: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Democratic Republic of the Congo
observations: Planting of the 2026 second-season maize crop was completed in January in northern and central regions and by the end of March in southern provinces.
Planting of the 2026 main maize season began in June in northern areas and was expected to begin in July in central regions.
FAO reports that conflict escalation in eastern provinces since late January 2025 has displaced people and restricted access to fields, disrupting agricultural activity.
The area planted to the 2026 main-season maize crop was estimated below the five-year average.
FAO reports maize and imported-rice prices remained elevated since January 2025, with tight market supply and high transport costs cited as contributing factors.
FAO estimated more than 26.5 million people severely acutely food insecure in 2026.
evidence.caveat: This is a food-security and seasonal outlook, not a completed national crop census, crop-cut yield series, or farm budget. The FAO brief page was returned in Spanish in the search result; verify the language/version and exact wording when citing in a public data interface.

evidence.source: World Bank indicator AG.YLD.CREL.KG, sourced from FAOSTAT
evidence.caveat: Aggregate cereal yield across cereals, not maize-, rice-, millet- or sorghum-specific yield. Do not use as a crop-specific enterprise yield.

evidence.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Production: Congo, Democratic Republic of the
evidence.caveat: These are USDA FAS estimates and marketing-year observations, not DRC national census measurements or verified final harvest totals. Do not mix marketing-year totals with calendar-year FAOSTAT values without reconciling definitions.

evidence.topic: USDA FAS corn yield and harvested area
evidence.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service production dashboard
evidence.caveat: Secondary international estimates. Check underlying USDA PS&D definitions and revisions before using. Rice yield was not extracted from this dashboard in the current review.

evidence.source: AKADEMIYA2063 Africa Agriculture Watch, Crop Production Forecasts Brief Series No. 137: DRC maize
evidence.caveat: Model-generated forecast based on remotely sensed geophysical data, not an official final production result. It differs from the USDA marketing-year series in scope and timing; do not average the estimates.

evidence.source: FAO GIEWS DRC Country Brief archive
observations: FAO described 2024 cereal production as affected by conflict, displacement, plant disease and rainfall impacts.
FAO reported that prices of beans, corn flour and rice in April 2024 were on average 50 percent higher than one year earlier and above the five-year average.
evidence.caveat: Historical price movement only; no absolute price level, district, quality grade or farm-gate price is provided in this summary. Do not treat this 2024 observation as a current 2026 price.

data_quality_and_use: DRC agricultural production is highly heterogeneous by province, season, transport access and security conditions; national averages are not a safe basis for farm-level profitability.

The current sources include FAO seasonal/food-security reporting, FAOSTAT-derived aggregate cereal yield, USDA marketing-year estimates and a model-based maize forecast. They are different evidence types and must remain separately labelled.
The current source set does not provide a verified, complete crop-specific national dataset with consistent area, production, yield and method across the major crops.
Conflict-related displacement and restricted field access can affect both agricultural production and the representativeness/recency of field observations.
No verified, dated province-level farm-gate prices, input costs or crop enterprise budgets were established in this review.
missing_data_before_calculator_use: Current province- and market-specific producer prices for maize, cassava, rice, beans, groundnuts, plantain/banana and horticultural crops, with date, grade, unit and price type.
Current input prices for seed, planting material, fertilizer, manure, crop protection, labour, land preparation, irrigation, fuel, machinery hire and transport.
Consistent crop-specific harvested area, production and yield series by province and season, with official methodology and revision history.
Crop calendars, planting density, crop duration, harvest frequency, marketable share, post-harvest losses and realistic farm-level yield distributions.
Province-specific logistics and security constraints affecting access to inputs, fields and markets.
Livestock production systems, breeds, herd/flock productivity, feed and veterinary costs, mortality and dated producer sale prices.
Validation of USDA and model-based estimates against DRC national statistical publications and any available agricultural survey or census tables.
recommendation: Retain DRC as research-only. Current evidence is useful for national context and broad crop production cross-checks, but source types, periods and geographic coverage are not sufficiently harmonized for a farm-profit calculator. Do not activate a country profile or derive farm profitability until official province-level crop data, dated farm-gate prices and input budgets are obtained and reconciled.
